In Table 2, the history-aggregation comparison (Section 5.3, p. 7):

- **GeM pooling** uses a **power mean**. Its update cost is $O(Kd)$, and it reaches MAR@100 of 0.447 (p. 7).
- **P-ATT** has an update cost of **$O(Kd)$**. Its operations are **positional encoding + dot product + softmax + weighted sum**. It reaches the highest MAR@100 in the table, 0.450 (p. 7).

The table caption adds that all history methods aggregate $K=10$ precomputed history embeddings of 1024 dimensions, and none of them need LLM re-inference during history updates (p. 7). The paper calls the margin between P-ATT and GeM "modest." It reads this as a sign that most of the benefit comes from adding recent behavioral context, not from a more expressive sequence model (p. 7).
